note: Ordinary moments already in a person's day (TAXONOMY.md §6). Each one declares what it OCCUPIES — what that moment makes unavailable — drawn from the `demands` facet in facets.json; an item fits when its demands and the moment's occupies do not intersect. Nothing here is scheduled — law 7: the app never schedules inside somebody's ritual, it offers what fits alongside it. Adding a moment is one row, and it matches the whole catalogue on arrival; no item is ever re-tagged.

opportunities.name: Sitting down
opportunities.typical: minutes at a time, many times a day

opportunities.name: Washing your hands
opportunities.note: Short, and it happens many times a day. The shortest real opportunity there is — which makes it the best teacher of the principle.

opportunities.name: Watching television
opportunities.note: The longest opportunity most people have, and the one that takes the least. Hands, room and floor are all free.

opportunities.name: Brushing your teeth
opportunities.note: One hand holds the brush; the other is free. So it blocks both-hands work and not one-handed work.

opportunities.name: In the shower
opportunities.note: Warm tissue. Better for range work than the same minutes anywhere else in the day.

opportunities.name: Waiting for the kettle
opportunities.note: Occupies nothing at all, which is why it was the founding example — and why naming a block after it hid the principle rather than teaching it (§6.1).
